images.title: Always even, or not always?
images.purpose: Shows the core move of the practice: factor out 2 to prove always even, or find one value that gives an odd result.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two cards side by side, one with a tick and one with a cross.
images.exact_structure: Two equal rounded cards side by side. Left card with a green (#009E73) outline: text 2a + 2b = 2(a + b) and below it a green (#009E73) tick with the words always even. Right card with a vermilion (#D55E00) outline: text 3g + 5h, under it g = 1, h = 2 gives 13, and below that a vermilion (#D55E00) cross with the words not always. Exactly 2 cards, 1 tick, 1 cross. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A factor of 2 proves always even; one odd example proves not always.
